title: Interactive Spend Forecast Widget and Token Handoff
creator: Avery Chen
description: Design and hand off an interactive Spend Forecast widget for the Redwood Console Cost Insights dashboard. The widget visualizes short- and long-term spend projections using multiple projection models, exposes adjustable knobs (time horizon, growth model, smoothing), and provides scenario snapshots that can be saved and compared. Deliverables: Figma component library for the widget (responsive variants), a token set for behavior-driven motion and color semantics, interaction specs (playback scrubber, hover affordances, keyboard accessibility), and a developer-ready redlines/spec sheet for engineering implementation.
design_notes: Primary goal: surface actionable spend projections while keeping the default state conservative and interpretable for non-financial users.
Support dual model types: deterministic rate-based projection (linear extrapolation) and probabilistic banded projection (Monte Carlo sketch with confidence bands).
Provide lightweight scenario builder: users can tweak 'expected growth %', 'seasonality factor', and 'one-off events' to see immediate projection deltas.

Motion tokenization: define three motion tokens (motion-fast, motion-medium, motion-soft) for scrubbing, band transitions, and tooltip fades so engineering can reuse the same timing across console animations.

Color token semantics: spend-up (brand-danger-60), spend-down (brand-success-50), baseline (neutral-600), forecast-band (neutral-100 with 24% opacity). Include token names that match existing token naming conventions to ease merge with design system.
Accessibility: ensure 4.5:1 contrast for forecast lines, keyboard operable scrubber with arrow and page keys, and ARIA live regions for scenario changes.
Responsive behavior: collapsed small-card variant showing single-line sparkline + compact delta; expanded panel shows full chart with controls and saved-scenarios list.
Performance note: prefer SVG path animations over canvas where possible to enable DOM tooling and accessibility hooks; provide fallback static images for very old browsers.
Trade-offs discussed: smoothing vs. raw token-level counters. We chose smoothing for default to reduce noise and offer a 'raw toggle' for power users.
Handoff format: Figma file with component variants + tokens page, a single-page redlines PDF, and a Storybook-ready JSON spec exported for engineering reference.
Risk: backend must expose time-series preview endpoints (lightweight sampling) to support instant previews; dependency ENG-4581 tracks the API work.
Metrics success: reduce user confusion tickets about "unexpected spikes" by 40% and increase usage of saved scenarios by 20% within first 6 weeks post-launch.
Open question: should saved scenarios be sharable via dashboard links or scoped to user only? PM to decide (see comments).
acceptance_criteria: Figma: Component library exists with responsive variants (card, panel) and documented tokens page.
Prototype: Interactive prototype in Figma demonstrating scrubber, scenario edits, and band toggles.
Handoff: Redlines PDF and token mapping (names + usage examples) delivered and linked in the ticket.
Accessibility: Keyboard interaction and ARIA labels documented; contrast checks pass for main chart elements.
Engineering: Frontend engineers can implement the widget against a 'preview' timeseries endpoint and match visual spec within 6px for key states.
UX Review: PM and two engineers have signed off on the behavior and API assumptions.
Observability: analytics events spec included for 'scenario_created', 'scenario_applied', 'forecast_hover', and 'save_snapshot'.

Token naming collision with global color tokens; mitigation: prefix tokens with 'forecast-' and coordinate merge with Design Systems team.
Scope creep: scenario sharing request may expand backend needs; PM decision to defer sharing until Q3.
